issues.description: The 'org admins update memberships' RLS policy on kontrolia_auth.memberships (migration 0010, untouched by any fix today) is FOR UPDATE USING (is_org_admin(organization_id)) with no column restriction — it permits changing ANY column on a membership row, including user_id, as long as organization_id itself is unchanged. None of prevent_last_owner_deactivation's checks (0026/0027) inspect user_id at all — they only compare status and organization_id. A plain org Admin can therefore UPDATE the sole active Owner's membership row, changing its user_id to an arbitrary existing platform user (who need not have had any prior relationship to the org), while leaving organization_id and status untouched. Since membership_roles is keyed by membership_id (not user_id), the Owner role instantly transfers to whoever the attacker chose. The original Owner ends up with zero membership rows in that org — a complete, silent lockout — while an arbitrary third party (attacker-controlled or otherwise) becomes the sole active Owner with no consent from anyone. The audit trigger log_membership_change() only inserts an audit_logs row when old.status IS DISTINCT FROM new.status, so a user_id-only change produces ZERO audit trail — this vector is not just unblocked but completely untraceable after the fact.

issues.description: kontrolia_auth.roles has zero triggers of any kind, and its own RLS policies ("org admins can create app-scoped custom roles" / "org admins can update custom roles", migration 0019) restrict only organization ownership and is_system_role — never the `slug` value a role may hold. Every last-owner/owner-grant guard added today (migrations 0025, 0028, 0029) and both permission helpers (is_org_owner, is_org_admin) identify "the Owner role" purely by string comparison against roles.slug = 'owner', with no check that the row is the canonical system role (organization_id IS NULL AND is_system_role = true, seeded once in migration 0004). This lets any plain org Admin — using only two individually ordinary, already-legitimate admin capabilities (create a custom app-scoped role for their own org; grant a non-owner role to themselves via the normal membership_roles path) — relabel a role they already hold into the trusted 'owner' string via a single UPDATE on kontrolia_auth.roles, a table none of today's five migrations (0025-0029) touch at all. This is a complete, orthogonal bypass of the entire day's last-owner-protection effort: it never inserts, updates, or deletes a membership_roles or memberships row in a way any of those triggers can see, because the row being mutated (kontrolia_auth.roles) is a different table entirely. Chained one step further, it enables a full, live-demonstrated organization takeover: once recognized as Owner via the hijacked role, the attacker causes migration 0025's active-owner count to read 2 (real Owner + hijacked-slug fake), which lets the attacker's ordinary membership_roles DELETE strip the real Owner's actual 'owner' role entirely, leaving the attacker as the sole recognized Owner and the real Owner with zero roles in the org — with no audit trail, since kontrolia_auth.log_role_assignment_change never fires for a roles.slug UPDATE.
evidence: Live query against information_schema.triggers on the running local Supabase Postgres (supabase_db_VACIO) confirms kontrolia_auth.roles has ZERO triggers of any kind — 0 rows returned.

packages/db/migrations/0019_app_scoped_custom_roles.sql — "org admins can create app-scoped custom roles" (INSERT) and "org admins can update custom roles" (UPDATE) policies on kontrolia_auth.roles check only organization_id/application_id presence, is_system_role, is_org_admin(organization_id), and (for INSERT) that application_organizations links the org+app — neither policy's WITH CHECK/USING expression mentions `slug` at all.

packages/db/migrations/0021_org_owner_delete.sql:9-24 (is_org_owner) and packages/db/migrations/0009_helper_functions.sql:19-36 (is_org_admin) both identify Owner/Admin purely via `r.slug = 'owner'` / `r.slug in ('owner','admin')` string comparison against whatever role row a membership_roles entry happens to point to, with no check that the role row is the canonical system role (organization_id IS NULL, is_system_role = true).

packages/db/migrations/0025_prevent_last_owner_role_removal.sql, 0028_restrict_owner_grant_and_membership_identity.sql, 0029_membership_roles_update_guard.sql — all three determine "is this an owner-role change" the same string-comparison way, and none of them place any trigger on kontrolia_auth.roles itself; their entire protection surface is membership_roles/memberships, a different table than the one this exploit mutates.

kontrolia_auth.log_role_assignment_change() (0013) fires on membership_roles INSERT/DELETE only — a roles.slug UPDATE (the actual exploit statement) is invisible to it, so the hijack itself produces zero audit_logs entry.
